Subject: Acme - Audit logging recap & next steps

Thanks Jill — great speaking with you and Tom earlier. Quick recap from today's demo + agreed next steps:

- Scope discussed: admin activity logs, API request/response logs, workspace/user-level access logs, and exportability for audits.
- Action items we agreed:
  1) I'll share a short overview of our audit logging capabilities (retention, export formats, immutability controls).
  2) We'll provide our latest SOC 2 report and a summary of GDPR/HIPAA controls.
  3) If you prefer, we can initiate the vendor security questionnaire and loop in our security team.

A few notes on the audit logs we demoed:
- Admin activity logs: records for user/admin actions (role changes, key rotations, policy updates) with timestamps and actor IDs.
- API logs: per-request metadata (request_id, endpoint, status code, latency, token usage) and partial request/response metadata (no full PII payloads by default; can be configured for debugging with safeguards).
- Exportability: logs can be exported as JSON/CSV via the Console or programmatically via our Export API; we also support scheduled S3 exports.
- Immutability: exports are generated from append-only storage with cryptographic checksums; for customers requiring WORM, we support write-once export buckets and signed audit bundles.

Attaching a short overview PDF. I'll drop the SOC 2 report and our security point-of-contact in a follow-up email.

Next steps: I'll send SOC 2 and start the vendor questionnaire after you confirm the preferred contact on your side (security@acmecorp.com or someone else).

Thanks,

Hi Jill — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers below and attaching our SOC 2 summary PDF.

- Retention: default retention is 90 days for detailed API logs and 365 days for admin activity logs. Retention is configurable per-tenant up to 7 years; we also support custom retention policies per log type via the Console or API.
- Export to customer S3: yes — we support scheduled and on-demand exports to customer-owned S3 buckets. For WORM/Object Lock use cases we recommend configuring the export bucket with Object Lock enabled; we sign the export bundle and provide checksum metadata (SHA-256) on each export for integrity verification.
- Immutability: logs are stored in append-only storage and exports include checksums and a signed manifest. For customers requiring strict immutability we support providing export bundles directly to a customer-managed WORM bucket and can coordinate proof-of-origin with our security team.

Attachments: SOC2-report-redwood-2026.pdf

If helpful, Neha from our security operations can jump on a call this week to walk through the export workflow and S3 setup. Marissa — should we schedule a 30-min call with Acme Security (Alex) and Neha?
